2. CONTENT: Graphene Raman spectra are conventionally reported in Raman shift (cm⁻¹), with the G peak canonically at ~1580–1585 cm⁻¹ and the 2D peak at ~2680–2700 cm⁻¹. This range is consistent with absolute wavelength in Å (580.0–710.0 nm) collected with a fixed excitation laser, from which Raman shift must be computed via the standard reciprocal formula:

Δν̃ (cm⁻¹) = 1e7/λ_laser(nm) − 1e7/λ_scattered(nm)

Testing the hypothesis: assume a common Raman excitation laser at 532 nm (a very standard green laser). Convert 532 nm to Å = 5320 Å — this is BELOW the data's minimum (5800 Å), which is impossible for Stokes scattering (scattered light must be at longer wavelength, i.e., higher Å, than the laser). So 532 nm is inconsistent with this window unless the laser is different.

1e7/532 = 18796.99 cm⁻¹ (laser wavenumber)
18796.99 − 1580 = 17216.99 cm⁻¹ (scattered wavenumber)
1e7/17216.99 = 580.85 nm = 5808.5 Å

Check: 5808.5 Å falls squarely inside the data's range [5800, 7100] Å, very near the low edge — consistent with the G peak appearing early in the scan, and 2D peak (~2700 cm⁻¹):
18796.99 − 2700 = 16096.99 cm⁻¹
1e7/16096.99 = 621.23 nm = 6212.3 Å — also inside range.

This confirms: laser = 532 nm, x-axis = absolute wavelength in Å, and the file must be converted to Raman shift (cm⁻¹) before the "G Peak" (a Raman-shift-domain concept) can be correctly identified.
